title: fix(fields)!: the record picker's display column labels a record the way the lookup dropdown does (objectui#10486)
body:
Fixes #10486
Clause-②: yes

The browse-all record picker's display column now labels a record exactly as the lookup dropdown's option label and the read cell do: through `@object-ui/core`'s `getRecordDisplayName`, with the same inputs and the same row. `RecordPickerDialog`'s published `titleFormat` prop is replaced by `objectSchema` (breaking; the changeset is `minor` under this repo's version policy).

## Authority

Ruling C1 on objectui#9436, verbatim (comment 5657441402, ratified in 5814246926):

> Ruling recorded — C1: `PageHeaderRenderer` aligns to the protocol — the declared pointer (`nameField` / `displayNameField`) outranks `titleFormat` in the header exactly as it does in `getRecordDisplayName`; the pin `titleFormat still outranks nameField` is rewritten to assert the opposite (director seat class-one adjudication, 2026-09-14)
>
> 1. In `PageHeaderRenderer`, the unified resolver (`getRecordDisplayName`) is consulted BEFORE the interpolated `titleFormat`; the template remains the fallback the contract assigns it — below the declared pointer, above bare record-key guesses.

The lookup branch of that ruling (objectui#10343, landed as PR objectui#10479) put the dropdown's option label on the order: the field's own `displayField`, then the object's `nameField`, then the deprecated `titleFormat`. The triage on this card (comment 5828316879), verbatim: 「route the column through the same `getRecordDisplayName` call as the dropdown and the read cell; ⛔ not a third copy of the ladder.」

## What changed

- `lookupColumnDisplay.tsx`: `LookupColumnRenderContext` carries `objectSchema` and `titleField` in place of `titleFormat`. Step 1 of `renderLookupColumnValue` renders `getRecordDisplayName(objectSchema, row, { titleField })` for the display column whenever a schema is given, not only when a template is declared. It uses `recordToOption`'s floor exclusion: an `Untitled` or `Record #id` answer is not a title, so the cell falls through to the column's own renderer. The private single-brace template renderer and its `EMPTY_SLOT` sentinel are deleted (0 readers left; `git grep` for `EMPTY_SLOT` and `refTitleFormat` under `packages/` exits 1, and the control `git grep -c renderLookupColumnValue` hits).
- `RecordPickerDialog.tsx`: the `titleFormat` prop is removed and `objectSchema` is added. `displayField` is now the DECLARED display field; the display column is keyed on `displayField ?? 'name'`, and only the declared value reaches the resolver as `titleField`. `renderCellContent` hands step 1 the same row as before (objectui#10223 / objectui#10373): relations collapsed by `toPredicateRecord`, fields the loaded policy denies removed by `withoutDeniedFields`. That is the row the dropdown's `recordToOption` labels from.
- `LookupField.tsx` (the one widened surface, in two spots only): the `refTitleFormat` memo is deleted, and the `RecordPickerDialog` JSX passes `displayField={declaredDisplayField}` and `objectSchema={refObjectSchema}`.
- The two pins that passed `titleFormat=` straight to the dialog now pass `objectSchema=` with unchanged assertions. They also drop their explicit `displayField="name"`: their rows carry a `name` value, so a declared `name` would rank above the template, which is what the migrated case means by "no declared display field". The pins are `LookupField.candidateExpand-10223` 'picker: same title cells, same task cells, same records handed to onSelectRecords' and `RecordPickerDialog.displayFls-10373` (its two `titleFormat` cases).
- New pins in `LookupField.pickerColumnOrder-10486.test.tsx`: each reads both surfaces off one mounted LookupField.

## Before and after (the new pins)

Fixture: fields `contract_no` / `name` / `account` / `short_code`; rows c1 = HT-001 / Acme / Globex / AC and c2 = HT-002 / Initech / Umbrella / IN.

| case | dropdown | picker column at base | picker column now |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `nameField: contract_no` + `titleFormat: '{account} / {contract_no}'` (agreement pin) | HT-001 | Globex / HT-001 | HT-001 |
| the same template in its double-brace spelling, no `nameField` | Globex / HT-001 | {Globex} / {HT-001} | Globex / HT-001 |
| single-brace template alone (lit control) | Globex / HT-001 | Globex / HT-001 | Globex / HT-001 |
| the lookup declares `displayField: short_code` | AC | Globex / HT-001 | AC |
| `nameField` only, rows carry `name` | HT-001 | Acme | HT-001 |
| `nameField` only, no `name` field | HT-001 | (blank) | HT-001 |

## Breaking change

`RecordPickerDialog` is re-exported from the `@object-ui/fields` entry, so its props are published. `titleFormat` is gone, with no dual spelling and no fallback built from it: pass `objectSchema`, the referenced object's schema, instead. Pass `displayField` only when the lookup declares one. The column also moves for `nameField`-only objects. Callers re-checked at `8740e86`: only `LookupField` passed `titleFormat` (the only non-test `titleFormat=` hit). `AccessExplainPanel`, `AssignedUsersSection` and `RelatedList` render the dialog without it and pass no `objectSchema`, so their display columns render exactly as before. `PeoplePicker` imports only `lookupFiltersToRecord`, and `LocationField` only names the dialog in a comment.

## Verification (head `3e3ad60`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/fields/` (through the verify lock): Test Files 201 passed, 1 skipped (202); Tests 3315 passed, 7 skipped; exit 0.
- `pnpm turbo run type-check --filter @object-ui/fields --concurrency=2`: Tasks 12 successful, 12 total; `@object-ui/fields:type-check` cache miss, executed; exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` includes the three touched test files.
- eslint on the 6 changed source and test files: 0 errors, 119 warnings, exit 0. Population: `ESLint.isPathIgnored` is false for 6 of 6. Count: `--format json` gives 6 results. Invariance: `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions` (no type-aware linting), and no `eslint-rules/` rule reads another file.
- Exit 0 for each of `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check:changeset-claims` (report-only), `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs` (6 source files of 1 released package, 1 changeset), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed` and `check-changeset-overwrite`.
- Reverse verification, one-shot, with the fix committed first (`20b031b`). The three implementation files were swapped to their `8740e86` blobs, and the swap was proven by the disk blob equalling the base blob for each file, plus marker counts: `getRecordDisplayName` 0 and `EMPTY_SLOT` 5 in `lookupColumnDisplay.tsx`. The new pin file plus the two migrated pins then ran: exit 1, 8 failed and 23 passed (31). Red: the five LookupField-mounted cases above other than the lit control, the unit control 'a record with a title renders it in the display column only', the objectui#10223 picker pin, and the objectui#10373 lit-control case. The restore (`git checkout HEAD --`, under a trap) was proven by the disk blob equalling the HEAD blob for all three files and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The same files at the fixed head: exit 0, 39 passed (five files). Predicted before the run: 9 red. Observed: 8 (see Acceptance notes).

## Acceptance notes

- The objectui#10373 case 'a `titleFormat` naming a denied field does not render it in the display column' stayed green under the reverse verification. Its expected cells equal what the column renders with no template at all. Its lit twin in the same file went red, so the pair still bites; the weakness predates this PR.
- Two pending changesets describe the tree before this change: the last paragraph of the objectui#10343 one (the picker column "still shows the template"), and the objectui#6874 one's `titleFormat={refTitleFormat}` sentence. This PR's changeset names both. A prose correction of those two files is outside the claimed surface and is left to the seat.
- The `withoutDeniedFields` doc comment in `LookupField.tsx` still says the picker applies the rule to "its display column's `titleFormat`". It now applies it to the display column's title. That comment sits outside the two fenced spots; noted, not edited.
- The floor test (`Untitled` / `Record #id`) is spelled out beside `recordToOption`'s and the read cell's. It is a floor check, not the ladder. Core exports no floor predicate, and `record-title.ts` is fenced.
- A probe of a declared `displayField` naming a relation, against a backend that does not honour `$expand`, read `[org1, org2]` in both the dropdown and the picker, at base and at this head, so no change was measured. The expanding-backend case is NOT MEASURED.
- The branch was merged with `origin/main` at `8740e86`. Six commits have landed on `main` since, and none touches `packages/fields` or the two changesets named above (`git diff --stat` is empty).
